grammar.countability: uncountable as a noun

usage.adjective: Use before a noun or after be, stay, or remain.
usage.noun: Use static without an indefinite article for radio noise or static electricity. A burst of static describes a short burst of noise.

en: (adjective) staying in the same position or remaining unchanged
(noun) crackling or hissing noise caused by interference in a signal
(noun) static electricity, especially in everyday speech
ja: （形容詞）動かない、変化しない、静的な
（名詞）ラジオなどの信号に混じるザーッ、バリバリという雑音
（名詞）静電気。日常会話での略称

nuance.en: Prices remained static means they stayed at the same level. A static image is still. In the expression static electricity, static refers to charge that has built up. As a noun, static can mean either the charge or the noise, depending on what you are talking about.
nuance.ja: Prices remained static. は「価格が同じ水準のままだった」。a static image は「動きのない画像」。static electricity の static は、電荷がたまっている状態を表す。名詞の static は文脈によって「静電気」や「ザザーッという雑音」になる。

en: stationary: Focuses on physical position. A stationary car is not moving. Static can describe things such as prices or design as well.
stagnant: Usually implies a lack of movement or growth that is undesirable. Sales remained static simply says they did not change. Sales were stagnant suggests a lack of progress.
static cling: The sticking effect caused by static electricity. Static on its own can name the charge behind the effect.
ja: stationary：物理的に動いていないことに焦点がある。a stationary car は「停止している車」。static は価格やデザインなどの変化の有無も表す。
stagnant：「停滞した」。変化や成長がないことを問題として捉える含みが出やすい。Sales remained static. は「売上が横ばいだった」という記述。
static cling：静電気による貼りつき。static 単独では、その原因となる静電気を指すことがある。

note.en: Close when describing a level, condition, or arrangement that stays the same.
note.ja: 水準や状態、配置が変化しないという意味で近い。

note.en: A broader term for disruption of a signal. Static is the noise you can hear.
note.ja: interference は信号の妨害を広く指す。static は耳に聞こえる雑音を指す。

etymology.en: The adjective is related to the idea of standing still. The electrical noun is short for static electricity.
etymology.ja: 形容詞の根にあるのは「じっと立っている、動かない」という考え方。静電気を指す名詞用法は static electricity を縮めたもの。

grammar.countability: countable as a noun, also commonly plural dynamics
patterns: the dynamic between A and B

usage.adjective: Before a noun, dynamic can mean energetic or changing in response to events or inputs.
usage.noun: A dynamic can describe a particular pattern of interaction. The plural dynamics often refers to several interacting forces or patterns.

en: (adjective) energetic, active, and able to make things happen
(adjective) changing or responding to conditions
(noun) a pattern of interaction or an influence that shapes how people or things interact
ja: （形容詞）活力のある、精力的な
（形容詞）変化する、状況に応じて変わる、動的な
（名詞）人や物事の相互作用、関係の中で働く力やそのパターン

nuance.en: A dynamic leader brings energy and initiative. Dynamic pricing changes in response to conditions such as demand. The dynamic between two people describes how they interact, including patterns such as who takes the lead.
nuance.ja: a dynamic leader は活力があり、自ら物事を進めるリーダー。dynamic pricing は需要などに応じて価格を変える仕組み。the dynamic between two people は、どちらが主導権を握るかなど、二人がどう影響し合うかを表す。

en: static: Staying the same or still. A static display stays fixed. A dynamic display can update as its inputs change.
energetic: Highlights energy and activity. Dynamic can also suggest initiative or the ability to drive change.
relationship: A broad term for a connection between people or groups. Dynamic focuses on how they interact within that relationship.
ja: static：動かない、変化しない。a static display は表示が固定されている。a dynamic display は入力などに応じて表示が変わりうる。
energetic：活力があることに焦点がある。dynamic には自ら動き、変化を起こすという含みも出る。
relationship：人や集団のつながりを広く指す。dynamic はその関係の中でどう影響し合うかに焦点がある。

note.en: Close when describing a person or team.
note.ja: 人やチームの活力を表す場合に近い。

note.en: Close when describing conditions that evolve over time.
note.ja: 時間とともに変化する状況を表す場合に近い。

etymology.en: Ultimately from Greek dynamis, meaning power or force.
etymology.ja: 「力」を表すギリシャ語 dynamis にさかのぼる。

word: like taking candy from a baby

patterns: it is / was like taking candy from a baby
verb-ing + be + like taking candy from a baby
as easy as taking candy from a baby

usage.register: Informal, especially American English. Often used to sum up how easily something was done, including a win over an opponent.
usage.form: After like, use taking. In this expression, candy is uncountable and a modifies baby.

en: extremely easy to do, often because there is little or no resistance
ja: いとも簡単にできる、拍子抜けするほどたやすい、朝飯前だ

nuance.en: The image is of taking candy from someone who can do little to stop you. It can sound playful when describing a game and boastful or dismissive when describing a real opponent. It can also describe taking advantage of someone who is easy to deceive.
nuance.ja: 赤ん坊からお菓子を取り上げるように、抵抗をほとんど受けずにできるというたとえ。ゲームの話なら冗談めいて聞こえるが、実際の対戦相手について言うと、自慢げだったり、相手を見下していたりするように響くことがある。だましやすい相手につけ込む場面でも使える。

en: a piece of cake: Says a task was very easy, often in a lighthearted way. Like taking candy from a baby can also suggest that an opponent could put up little resistance.
a walk in the park: Often describes a task or experience that takes little effort or causes little trouble.
ja: a piece of cake：「朝飯前だ」。作業の簡単さを気軽に言う表現。like taking candy from a baby には、相手がほとんど抵抗できなかったという含みも出る。
a walk in the park：「楽なこと」。手間や苦労がほとんどない作業や経験についてよく使う。

note.en: A common informal expression for something very easy.
note.ja: 「とても簡単なこと」を表す口語表現。

etymology.en: The idiom draws on the image of how little effort it would take to take candy away from a baby.
etymology.ja: 赤ん坊からお菓子を取り上げるのにほとんど労力が要らない、というたとえ。

en: I thought the final round would be tough, but it was like taking candy from a baby.

ja: I thought the final round would be tough, but it was like taking candy from a baby. — 最終ラウンドは苦戦すると思っていたけれど、拍子抜けするほど簡単だった。

usage.adverb: Often comes after the verb or its object. Stay overnight has no object, and leave the dough overnight has the dough as its object.
usage.adjective: Usually comes before a noun, as in an overnight flight or an overnight success.
usage.verb: Can mean to stay somewhere for a night or, especially in US shipping, to send something for next-day delivery.

en: (adverb / adjective) for one night or during the night
(adverb / adjective) with arrival or delivery by the next day
(adverb / adjective) very quickly or suddenly, sometimes figuratively
(verb) to stay somewhere for a night, or to send something for next-day delivery
ja: （副詞・形容詞）一晩、夜の間に、一泊の
（副詞・形容詞）翌日までに、翌日着の
（副詞・形容詞）一夜にして、急に、あっという間に
（動詞）一泊する、翌日着で送る

nuance.en: Stay overnight describes spending the night somewhere. It snowed overnight means that snow fell during the night. An overnight delivery is scheduled for the next day. In Nothing will change overnight, overnight means very quickly and need not refer to a literal night.
nuance.ja: stay overnight は「一泊する」。It snowed overnight. は「夜の間に雪が降った」。overnight delivery は「翌日配達」。Nothing will change overnight. の overnight は比喩的に「すぐには」を表し、実際に一晩という時間を示すとは限らない。

en: all night: Emphasizes that an activity or state continued throughout the night. It rained overnight leaves the duration of the rain open. It rained all night says it continued through the night.
the next day: Identifies when something happened. Overnight often highlights the interval, speed or delivery arrangement that brings something to the next day.
suddenly: Highlights an abrupt change. Overnight can emphasize how little time a development took, as in become an overnight success.
ja: all night：「一晩中」。It rained overnight. は夜の間に雨が降ったというだけで、降り続いた時間は分からない。It rained all night. は夜通し降ったという意味。
the next day：「その翌日」。出来事がいつ起きたかを示す。overnight は、翌日までの時間の短さや翌日着の手配を表すことがある。
suddenly：「突然」。変化の急さを強調する。overnight は an overnight success（あっという間の成功）のように、結果が出るまでの短さにも焦点を当てる。

note.en: Close when an event happens between evening and morning.
note.ja: 出来事が夜の間に起きたことを表す場合に近い。

note.en: Close in the figurative sense.
note.ja: 「あっという間に」という比喩的な用法で近い。

etymology.en: A compound of over and night, referring to the span from one evening into the following morning.
etymology.ja: over と night の複合語。夜をまたいで翌朝に至る時間を表す。

grammar.countability: countable as a noun

usage.noun: Use a household for one person living alone or a group living together as one domestic unit.
usage.modifier: Before a noun, household can mean related to the home, its occupants, or everyday domestic use.

en: (noun) one person living alone or a group of people living together as a domestic unit
(adjective) connected with the home or the people who live in it, or intended for use in the home
ja: （名詞）世帯。一人暮らしの人、または一緒に暮らす人たちを生活の単位として捉えたもの
（形容詞）家庭の、家計の、家庭用の

nuance.en: Household looks at who lives together as a unit. A person living alone can be a one-person household, and a household may include people who are unrelated. Household income and per household are common when counting or comparing domestic units. Household chores are jobs done around the home. A household name is a person, brand, or other name widely recognized by the public.
nuance.ja: household は、一緒に暮らす人たちを生活の単位として捉える。単身世帯もあり、血縁関係のない人を含むこともある。household income（世帯収入）や per household（一世帯あたり）は、世帯単位で数えたり比較したりするときによく使う。household chores は「日常の家事」。a household name は、世間に広く知られている人やブランドなどを指す。

en: family: Focuses on family ties, which can extend across several households. Household focuses on a living arrangement or domestic unit.

home: Often refers to the place where someone lives. Home insurance is insurance connected with the property or its contents. Household expenses are the living expenses of the people in the household.
domestic: Can mean connected with home life or, in expressions such as domestic flights, within one country. Household income is tied specifically to a domestic unit.
ja: family：親族や家族としてのつながりに焦点がある。一つの family が複数の household に分かれて暮らすこともある。household は生活の単位としての世帯に焦点がある。
home：暮らす場所を指すことが多い。home insurance は住宅や家財に関する保険。household expenses は世帯の生活費。
domestic：「家庭の」のほか、domestic flights（国内便）のように「国内の」という意味もある。household income は「世帯収入」。

note.en: Close when modifying a noun related to home life or home use.
note.ja: 家庭生活や家庭での用途に関する語を修飾するときに近い。

etymology.en: A compound of house and hold, referring to a home and the people belonging to it.
etymology.ja: house と hold の複合語。家と、そこに属する人々を指す語。

grammar.countability: countable, often plural for routine duties
patterns: something is / feels like a chore

usage.routine: Use chores in the plural for routine duties collectively. Use a chore for an individual job or for an activity that feels tedious.

en: a small job that needs doing regularly, especially around the home
a task that feels tedious, unpleasant, or burdensome
ja: 定期的にこなす雑用、特に日常の家事
面倒で気の進まない作業、骨の折れる用事

nuance.en: Household chores groups together recurring jobs such as doing laundry or taking out the trash. It can be a neutral label. Calling something a chore emphasizes how tedious it feels, even when it has nothing to do with housework.
nuance.ja: household chores は、洗濯やゴミ出しなど繰り返し行う家事の総称で、中立的にも使える。何かを a chore と呼ぶと、その作業が億劫だという気持ちがにじむ。家事以外の作業についても使える。

en: task: A broad word for a piece of work. Chore often suggests routine upkeep or something you find tedious.
housework: An uncountable word for work done to look after a home. Chore is countable and can name one of the individual jobs.
errand: Often a short trip to do something, such as picking up a prescription. A chore can be done at home, like folding laundry.
ja: task：作業一般を指す。chore は日々の維持に必要な仕事や、面倒に感じる作業を指すことが多い。
housework：家を維持するための仕事をまとめて指す不可算名詞。chore は可算名詞で、個々の作業も数えられる。
errand：処方薬を受け取りに行くなど、外出を伴うちょっとした用事。chore は洗濯物をたたむなど、家の中でする作業にも使える。

note.en: Close for a recurring job that needs to be done.
note.ja: 繰り返しこなす必要がある仕事を表す場合に近い。

etymology.en: A variant of char, an older word for an odd job. Its earlier forms included Middle English cherre and Old English cerr, meaning a turn or occasion.

usage.noun: Often denotes a wood managed by regularly cutting back trees. It may also refer more generally to a small wood or thicket.
usage.verb: Transitive. A species or area can be the object, as in coppice the hazel or coppice part of the woodland.

en: (noun) a small wood or stand, especially one managed by repeatedly cutting back trees to obtain new growth and wood
(verb) to cut a tree or shrub back close to the ground so that new shoots grow from the base
ja: （名詞）小さな雑木林。特に、木を周期的に切り戻し、株からの新芽を育てて木材を得る林
（動詞）木や低木を地際まで切り戻し、株から新芽を出させる。萌芽更新を行う

nuance.en: In woodland management, coppicing leaves a living stump called a stool. New shoots grow from it and can be harvested later. A hazel coppice is a stand of hazel managed in this way.
nuance.ja: 林の管理では、切り戻した後に生きた株（stool）を残し、そこから伸びた新しい枝や幹を後に収穫する。a hazel coppice は、この方法で管理するハシバミの林。

en: copse: A general word for a small group of trees or a small wood. Coppice, especially in forestry, often implies repeated cutting and regrowth.
pollard: To cut back a tree higher up on the trunk so that new shoots grow above ground. Coppicing cuts close to ground level.
prune: A general term for trimming or removing parts of a plant. Coppice names a particular way of cutting for regrowth from the base.
ja: copse：小さな林や木立を広く指す。coppice は林業では、繰り返し切って新芽を育てる管理を含意することが多い。
pollard：幹の高い位置で切り戻し、地面から離れた位置に新しい枝を出させる。coppice は地際で切り戻す。
prune：枝などを切る、剪定するという広い表現。coppice は株元から再生させるための特定の切り方を指す。

note.en: Close for a small wood in the general noun sense.
note.ja: 名詞で小さな林を広く指す場合に近い。

etymology.en: From Old French copeiz or coupeiz, referring to a wood where trees had been cut. The English word copse developed as a shortened form of coppice.
etymology.ja: 木を伐った林を指す古フランス語 copeiz または coupeiz に由来する。英語の copse は coppice の短縮形から生まれた。

usage.register: Informal. It can describe managing an event, leading a group, or exercising practical control over how things are done.
usage.form: The verb run changes with the tense. Keep the show in the usual idiom.

en: to be in charge of a group, event, or operation and direct how things are done
ja: 物事を仕切る、指揮を執る、中心となって運営する

nuance.en: Run the show is conversational and often emphasizes who is actually directing the work or making decisions. It can be neutral, admiring, or critical depending on the context. The person running the show can be the official leader or someone whose influence is informal.
nuance.ja: run the show は口語的で、実際に誰が取りまとめ、決定を下しているかに焦点を当てることが多い。文脈によって、単に担当者を示したり、手腕を評価したり、仕切りすぎだと批判したりできる。正式な責任者にも、肩書きはなくても実質的に動かしている人にも使える。

en: be in charge of: A neutral way to describe responsibility. Run the show gives a more conversational sense of actively directing what happens.
call the shots: Emphasizes who makes the decisions. Run the show can include coordinating people and making sure the operation works.
take over: Focuses on the point when someone assumes control. Run the show describes what they do once they are in control.
ja: be in charge of：「～を担当する、～の責任者である」という中立的な表現。run the show は口語的で、実際に物事を動かしている感じが出る。
call the shots：「決定権を握る」。誰が決めるかに重点がある。run the show は人の調整や運営全体を回すことも含む。
take over：「引き継ぐ、主導権を引き取る」。主導権が移る時点に焦点がある。run the show は主導権を持って仕切っていることを表す。

note.en: A more neutral expression for being responsible for something.
note.ja: 物事の責任者であることを示す、より中立的な表現。

etymology.en: The expression uses the image of someone running a show as a metaphor for directing any group or operation.
etymology.ja: 公演を取り仕切る人をイメージに、組織や活動を仕切ることを表した言い方。

run the show behind the scenes
run the whole show
let someone run the show

run the whole show — 全体を取り仕切る

usage.register: Informal American English. Cry uncle is a common variant. The imperative Say uncle! demands that the other person concede.
usage.form: The idiom uses uncle without an article. The verb say changes with tense.

en: to give in or concede defeat, especially after resisting or under pressure
ja: 参ったと認める、降参する、抵抗していたがついに折れる

nuance.en: Say uncle can be playful in games or challenges. In an argument or negotiation, it can imply that someone resisted and ultimately yielded to pressure. Say uncle! means ‘Admit you’ve had enough!’ or ‘Give up!’ depending on the situation.
nuance.ja: 遊びや勝負では冗談めいて使える。議論や交渉で使うと、抵抗していた人が押し切られて折れた、という含みが出る。命令形 Say uncle! は場面に応じて「参ったって言え！」「降参しろ！」に当たる。

en: give in: A broader, more neutral expression for yielding to pressure or agreeing after resisting.
give up: Can mean to stop trying or abandon an effort, even when there is no opponent. Say uncle often suggests conceding to an opponent or pressure.
throw in the towel: Highlights deciding to stop trying. Say uncle often highlights admitting that you have been beaten or giving in.
ja: give in：「折れる、譲る」を表す広く中立的な言い方。
give up：「諦める、やめる」。相手がいない場合にも使える。say uncle には、相手やその場の圧力に屈するという響きが出やすい。
throw in the towel：「これ以上続けない」と決めることに重点がある。say uncle は負けを認めたり、折れたりするところに焦点がある。

note.en: A variant of the same informal US idiom.
note.ja: 同じ意味のアメリカ英語の口語表現。

note.en: A straightforward way to say that someone acknowledges losing.
note.ja: 「負けを認める」をそのまま表す言い方。

etymology.en: The expression is associated with using the word uncle as a signal of surrender in rough play. The reason uncle became the surrender word is uncertain.
etymology.ja: じゃれ合いなどで uncle を降参の合図として言わせる使い方と結びついている。なぜ uncle が降参の合図になったかには諸説がある。

en: Say uncle!
finally say uncle
refuse to say uncle
make someone say uncle
cry uncle
ja: Say uncle! — 参ったって言え！
finally say uncle — ついに折れる
refuse to say uncle — 降参するのを拒む
make someone say uncle — 相手に参ったと言わせる
cry uncle — 降参する、参ったと認める

en: I thought I could do one more round, but after twenty minutes I finally said uncle.
The other side kept pushing for a discount, but we refused to say uncle.
“Say uncle!” my brother said. “Okay, okay. You win.”
ja: I thought I could do one more round, but after twenty minutes I finally said uncle. — もう１ラウンドいけると思ったけど、20分たってとうとう参ったと認めた。
The other side kept pushing for a discount, but we refused to say uncle. — 先方は値引きを求め続けたが、こちらは折れなかった。
“Say uncle!” my brother said. “Okay, okay. You win.” — 兄が「参ったって言え！」と言った。「分かった、分かった。そっちの勝ちだよ」

usage.speech: Common in written dialogue and narration, where it identifies an utterance as a sudden or emphatic reaction. It can also introduce a that-clause.

en: to say something suddenly or emphatically, often because of surprise, delight, anger, or another strong feeling
ja: 驚きや喜び、怒りなどで思わず声を上げる、感情を込めて言う

nuance.en: Exclaim draws attention to the reaction expressed in the words. It is particularly common as a reporting verb in stories. Someone can shout to be heard across a room. Someone who exclaims ‘That’s impossible!’ is reacting with strong feeling.
nuance.ja: exclaim は、発した言葉に表れる感情の強さやとっさの反応に焦点を当てる。特に物語のセリフに添える動詞としてよく使う。部屋の向こうに声を届けるためなら shout が自然。思わず「そんなはずがない！」と声を上げる場面なら exclaim が合う。

en: shout: Emphasizes speaking or calling loudly. The reason can be practical, such as distance or background noise.
cry out: Can describe a sudden sound without words, such as a cry of pain. Exclaim is often used to introduce the actual words spoken.
claim: Means to assert that something is true or to demand something you believe is yours. Exclaim describes the manner of speaking.
ja: shout：大きな声で言う、呼びかける。距離が遠かったり、周りが騒がしかったりして声を張る場合にも使う。
cry out：痛みで声を上げるなど、言葉になっていない声にも使う。exclaim は発した言葉を引用するときによく使う。
claim：「～だと主張する」「権利があるものを請求する」。exclaim は言い方や感情の表れを描く。

note.en: Close when someone speaks suddenly in reaction to something.
note.ja: 何かに反応してとっさに声を上げる意味で近い。

etymology.en: Ultimately from Latin exclamare, ‘to cry out’, formed from ex- and clamare, ‘to shout or call’.
etymology.ja: ラテン語 exclamare（声を上げる）にさかのぼる。ex- と clamare（叫ぶ、呼ぶ）から成る。

en: exclaim in surprise
exclaim with delight
exclaim in disbelief
exclaim that something is impossible
ja: exclaim in surprise — 驚いて声を上げる
exclaim with delight — 喜びで声を上げる
exclaim in disbelief — 信じられないという様子で声を上げる
exclaim that something is impossible — そんなことはあり得ないと声を上げる

en: “You made this yourself?” she exclaimed.
“We got the grant!” he exclaimed as he read the email.
When I told him the price, he exclaimed that it was more than twice what he had paid last year.
ja: “You made this yourself?” she exclaimed. — 「これ、自分で作ったの？」と彼女は驚いて声を上げた。
“We got the grant!” he exclaimed as he read the email. — メールを読んだ彼は「助成金が取れたぞ！」と喜びの声を上げた。
When I told him the price, he exclaimed that it was more than twice what he had paid last year. — 値段を伝えると、彼は「去年払った額の倍以上じゃないか！」と声を上げた。

usage.transitive: Use a noun for the outcome, as in ensure continuity, or a clause, as in ensure that the files are backed up. That can be omitted.

en: to make certain that something happens or that a condition is met
ja: 必要な結果が得られるようにする、条件が満たされるようにする、確保する

nuance.en: Ensure often appears in instructions, policies, and formal writing. It can involve checking a condition, taking action to bring it about, or putting a safeguard in place. In Please ensure that all attachments are included, the recipient is responsible for making sure nothing is missing.
nuance.ja: ensure は指示書や規程など、やや改まった文でよく使う。確認したり、必要な措置を取ったりして、望ましい状態を確実にするという意味。Please ensure that all attachments are included. は、添付漏れがないよう確認し、不足があればそろえるところまで求める指示。

en: assure: Usually takes a person as its object when it means to give someone confidence. I assured her that we would meet the deadline. Ensure takes the outcome or a clause.
insure: Most commonly means to cover someone or something with insurance. In US English it can also mean ensure.
make sure: A common everyday way to express the same idea. Make sure (that) the door is locked is natural in conversation. Ensure (that) the door is locked fits written instructions.
ja: assure：「～だと伝えて安心させる、断言する」の意味では、I assured her that we would meet the deadline. のように相手が目的語になる。ensure は確実にしたい結果を名詞や節で表す。
insure：「保険をかける、保険で補償する」が主な意味。米国英語では ensure と同じ意味でも使われる。
make sure：日常的な「確かめる、確実にする」。鍵がかかっていることを求めるなら、会話では Make sure the door is locked.、書面の指示では Ensure that the door is locked. が自然。

note.en: A common equivalent, especially before a clause.
note.ja: 特に節を伴う場合に近い日常表現。

note.en: Close when something makes an outcome certain. Guarantee can also refer to a promise.
note.ja: 結果を確実にする意味で近い。guarantee には約束や保証をする用法もある。

etymology.en: From Anglo-French enseurer, formed from en- ‘make’ and Old French seur ‘sure’.
etymology.ja: アングロ・フランス語 enseurer に由来する。「～にする」を表す en- と、古フランス語 seur（確かな）から成る。

en: ensure safety
ensure compliance with the rules
ensure equal access
ensure a smooth transition
ensure that the deadline is met
ja: ensure safety — 安全を確保する
ensure compliance with the rules — 規則が守られるようにする
ensure equal access — 平等に利用できるようにする
ensure a smooth transition — 円滑に移行できるようにする
ensure that the deadline is met — 期限を守れるようにする

en: Please ensure that all attachments are included before filing the application.
We added a second review to ensure that no changes were overlooked.
A backup system helps ensure that the service remains available during maintenance.
ja: Please ensure that all attachments are included before filing the application. — 出願書類を提出する前に、添付書類がすべてそろっていることを確認してください。
We added a second review to ensure that no changes were overlooked. — 変更点の見落としを防ぐため、二度目のレビューを追加した。
A backup system helps ensure that the service remains available during maintenance. — 予備システムがあれば、メンテナンス中もサービスを利用できる状態を保ちやすい。

usage.reason: Either a person or the reason itself can be the subject. We justified the expense explains our action. The savings justify the expense gives the reason it makes sense.
usage.typography: In word processors, Justify usually means aligning text to both margins. Left-justify and right-justify specify a single margin.

en: to give or constitute a good reason for an action, decision, or cost
to explain why your own actions or choices were reasonable
to align typeset text with a margin or with both margins
ja: 行動・判断・費用などに十分な理由を示す、十分な理由となる、正当化する
自分の行動や選択が妥当だった理由を説明する
文章を左右の余白に合わせて揃える。文書編集の Justify は通常「両端揃え」

nuance.en: Justify asks whether the reason is good enough to make something acceptable or worthwhile. The savings justify the cost means the savings make the expense worthwhile. Justify can be neutral in budgeting or analysis. Justify yourself can sound defensive when someone has questioned your actions.
nuance.ja: justify の焦点は、ある行為や判断が妥当だと言えるだけの理由があるかどうか。The savings justify the cost. は「節約効果を考えれば、費用をかける価値がある」。予算や分析の文脈では中立的に使え、justify yourself は、自分の行動を問われて弁明するような響きが出ることもある。

en: explain: Makes the reason or cause clear. Explaining why a delay happened gives its cause. Justifying the delay gives a reason to consider it acceptable.
warrant: A more formal word for being sufficient grounds for an action. The evidence warrants further investigation means it is strong enough to call for further investigation.
rationalize: In the sense of explaining behavior, it often suggests inventing a plausible excuse for a decision already made. Justify can be used for a genuinely good reason.
ja: explain：理由や原因を明らかにする。遅れを explain するのは原因を説明すること。遅れを justify するのは、その遅れがやむを得ないといえる根拠を示すこと。
warrant：「～するに足る根拠となる」という改まった表現。The evidence warrants further investigation. は「その証拠は追加調査を行うに足る」という意味。
rationalize：行動の説明については、すでに下した判断にもっともらしい理由を後づけする含みが出やすい。justify は、十分な根拠が本当にある場合にも使う。

note.en: Close when a fact or benefit provides sufficient grounds for doing something.
note.ja: ある事実や利点が、何かをするに足る根拠となる場合に近い。

note.en: Close when someone gives reasons for a decision being challenged.
note.ja: 異議を唱えられた判断について、理由を示して擁護するときに近い。

etymology.en: From Old French justifiier, ultimately from Late Latin iustificare. Its Latin elements go back to iustus, ‘just’, and facere, ‘to make or do’.
etymology.ja: 古フランス語 justifiier を経て、後期ラテン語 iustificare にさかのぼる。もとになるのは iustus（公正な、正しい）と facere（作る、行う）。

en: justify a decision
justify the cost
justify the use of force
justify spending more
justify yourself
be justified in asking for proof
the end justifies the means
justify the text
ja: justify a decision — 判断の妥当性を説明する
justify the cost — 費用に見合う理由になる、費用をかける根拠を示す
justify the use of force — 武力行使を正当化する
justify spending more — 追加支出の妥当性を示す
justify yourself — 自分の行動を弁明する
be justified in asking for proof — 証拠を求めるだけの理由がある
the end justifies the means — 目的が手段を正当化する
justify the text — 文章を両端揃えにする

en: The time savings alone don’t justify the cost of switching systems.
How can we justify charging customers for a feature they already had?
Given the conflicting reports, she was justified in asking for more evidence.
The template justifies the body text and centers the headings.
ja: The time savings alone don’t justify the cost of switching systems. — 時間の節約だけでは、システムを切り替える費用に見合わない。
How can we justify charging customers for a feature they already had? — 顧客がすでに使えていた機能を有料にすることを、どう正当化できるだろうか。
Given the conflicting reports, she was justified in asking for more evidence. — 報告の内容が食い違っていたので、彼女が追加の証拠を求めたのはもっともだった。
The template justifies the body text and centers the headings. — そのテンプレートは本文を両端揃えにし、見出しを中央揃えにする。

grammar.countability: countable or uncountable (reason or grounds) / uncountable (typography)
patterns: there is no justification for + noun / -ing

usage.countability: Use a justification for one identifiable reason or defense, and no or little justification when speaking of grounds in general.
usage.preposition: Justification for the decision is the reason supporting it. Justification of the decision can refer to the act or process of defending it.

en: a reason or set of grounds that makes an action, decision, or belief seem reasonable or acceptable
the act of showing that something is reasonable, acceptable, or warranted
the alignment of typeset text with one or both margins, especially both margins
ja: 行動・判断・信念などを妥当と認めるための理由、根拠
ある行動や判断などの妥当性を示すこと、正当化
組版や文書編集で文字を余白に合わせて揃えること、特に両端揃え

nuance.en: Justification focuses on whether there are good enough grounds to accept a decision, practice, or expense. A justification may be requested in a routine review, and no justification for can express strong criticism. A justification someone offers may still be disputed.
nuance.ja: 判断・慣行・支出などを妥当と認めるに足る根拠に焦点がある。予算審査で根拠を求めるような中立的な場面にも、no justification for で強く非難する場面にも使う。相手が示した根拠を a justification と呼び、その十分性を争うこともできる。

en: explanation: An account of how or why something happened. A missed deadline may have an explanation and still lack sufficient justification.
rationale: The reasoning behind a choice or design. Justification emphasizes whether there are sufficient grounds to accept it.
excuse: A reason offered to reduce blame, often with a suggestion that the reason is weak. Justification can be a sound, evidence-based defense.
ja: explanation：なぜ、あるいはどう起きたかを明らかにする説明。締切に遅れた経緯を説明できても、遅れを容認できるだけの根拠があるかは別の問題。
rationale：選択や設計の背景にある考え方。justification は、その選択を妥当と認めるに足る根拠に重点がある。
excuse：非難を和らげるための弁明や言い訳。理由が弱いという含みを帯びやすい。justification は証拠に裏づけられた妥当な根拠にも使える。

note.en: Close when referring to the basis that warrants a decision or action, especially in formal contexts.
note.ja: 判断や行動を支える根拠を指すときに近く、特に改まった文脈で使う。

note.en: Close when someone responds to criticism by explaining why a choice was reasonable.
note.ja: 批判に応じて選択の妥当性を説明し、擁護する場合に近い。

etymology.en: A noun in the same word family as justify (verb) and justifiable (adjective).
etymology.ja: justify（動詞）、justifiable（形容詞）と同じ語族に属する名詞。

en: provide a justification for the decision
offer little justification for the expense
there is no justification for the delay
without adequate justification
a compelling justification
a written justification
in justification of the decision
full justification
ja: provide a justification for the decision — 判断の妥当性を示す理由を提示する
offer little justification for the expense — その支出を妥当とする根拠をほとんど示していない
there is no justification for the delay — その遅れを正当化できる理由はない
without adequate justification — 十分な根拠を欠いたまま
a compelling justification — 説得力のある根拠
a written justification — 根拠を記した書面
in justification of the decision — その判断の妥当性を示すために

usage.sense: With a person or reaction, indulgent suggests a willingness to overlook faults or grant wishes. With food or an experience, it suggests a treat that feels rich or luxurious.

en: inclined to let someone have what they want or to overlook their faults
showing affectionate or amused tolerance
rich, luxurious, or especially pleasurable in the way a treat is
ja: 人の望みをかなえてやったり、欠点や失敗を大目に見たりする、甘い、寛大な
優しく、あるいはおかしみを感じながら大目に見るような
食べ物や体験などが、濃厚で贅沢な、ごほうび感のある

nuance.en: An indulgent parent may be affectionately generous or overly permissive, depending on context. An indulgent smile can show fond amusement. In food writing and advertising, an indulgent dessert is usually something rich and pleasurable, and the word is often used approvingly.
nuance.ja: an indulgent parent は、愛情から子どもの望みを聞いてやる親にも、甘やかしすぎる親にも使える。an indulgent smile は、相手の言動をほほえましく思って浮かべる笑み。食や広告の文脈では、an indulgent dessert のように、濃厚で贅沢な楽しみを表す好意的な表現としてよく使う。

en: lenient: Mild in judging or punishing someone. Indulgent can also suggest actively giving someone what they want.
permissive: Allows a great deal of freedom, especially through loose rules. Indulgent can have a warmer, more affectionate tone.
self-indulgent: Focuses on gratifying one's own desires and often sounds critical. An indulgent dessert describes the treat itself and can be praised.
ja: lenient：判断や処分が寛大な。indulgent には、相手の望みを積極的にかなえてやる含みもある。
permissive：規則やしつけが緩く、自由にさせる。indulgent には相手への愛情や、その相手に対する甘さがにじむことがある。
self-indulgent：自分の欲を満たすことに甘く、批判的に響きやすい。an indulgent dessert はデザート自体を贅沢なごほうびとして好意的に表現できる。

note.en: Close when someone overlooks faults or is mild in their judgment.
note.ja: 欠点を大目に見たり、判断が寛大だったりする場合に近い。

note.en: Close in food descriptions, often emphasizing rich or extravagant pleasure.
note.ja: 食べ物の描写で近く、とりわけ濃厚でぜいたくな楽しみを強調する。

etymology.en: Related to the verb indulge and the noun indulgence.
etymology.ja: indulge（動詞）、indulgence（名詞）と同じ語族。

en: an indulgent parent
an indulgent smile
be indulgent toward one's grandchildren
an indulgent dessert
a rich, indulgent treat
an indulgent weekend away
ja: an indulgent parent — 子どもに甘い親
an indulgent smile — ほほえましそうな笑み
be indulgent toward one's grandchildren — 孫に甘い
an indulgent dessert — 贅沢なデザート
a rich, indulgent treat — 濃厚で贅沢なごほうび
an indulgent weekend away — 旅先で贅沢に過ごす週末

en: My grandparents were indulgent with me and always let me stay up past my bedtime.
She gave him an indulgent smile when he launched into the same story again.
The chocolate tart is wonderfully indulgent, especially with a spoonful of whipped cream.
ja: My grandparents were indulgent with me and always let me stay up past my bedtime. — 祖父母は私に甘く、いつも寝る時間を過ぎても起きていていいと言ってくれた。
She gave him an indulgent smile when he launched into the same story again. — 彼がまた同じ話を始めると、彼女はほほえましそうに笑った。
The chocolate tart is wonderfully indulgent, especially with a spoonful of whipped cream. — そのチョコレートタルトはとても贅沢な味わいで、ホイップクリームをひとさじ添えると格別だ。

patterns: can't / won't put up with + noun

usage.wordOrder: Keep put up with together before its object, as in put up with it. A question can end in with, as in What do you have to put up with?

en: to tolerate an unpleasant person, thing, or situation, especially when it persists or happens repeatedly
ja: 不快な人・物事・状況を我慢する、嫌なことに耐える。特に長引いたり繰り返されたりする場合によく使う

nuance.en: Put up with is common in conversation and often conveys irritation or reluctant acceptance. I can't put up with it anymore says the speaker has reached their limit. I won't put up with it expresses a decision to stop accepting it.
nuance.ja: 会話でよく使い、不満を抱えながらも受け入れている感じが出やすい。I can't put up with it anymore. は「もう我慢の限界だ」。I won't put up with it. は「そんなことは許さない、黙って受け入れるつもりはない」という意思を表す。

en: tolerate: A close single-word equivalent that also fits formal statements and policies. Put up with sounds conversational and often conveys personal annoyance.
endure: Often suggests lasting through hardship, sometimes severe. Put up with is common for everyday annoyances.
deal with: Can mean handling or addressing a problem. Put up with focuses on tolerating it while it continues.
ja: tolerate：意味が近い一語の動詞で、声明や規則など改まった文脈にも合う。put up with は会話的で、個人的な不満がにじみやすい。
endure：苦痛や困難に耐え抜く意味合いがあり、深刻な状況にも使う。put up with は日常の迷惑によく使う。
deal with：問題に対処する、処理する。put up with は、問題が続く中でそれを我慢することに焦点がある。

note.en: The closest general equivalent for accepting something unpleasant.
note.ja: 不快なことを許容するという意味で近い。

note.en: Especially close in the negative, as in I can't stand the noise.
note.ja: I can't stand the noise. のような否定文で特に近い。

etymology.en: A fixed expression built from put, up, and with. It is useful to learn the three words together.
etymology.ja: put、up、with からなる定型表現。3語をひとまとまりとして覚えると使いやすい。

equivalents.de: etwas ertragen / sich etwas gefallen lassen

en: put up with the noise
put up with rude behavior
put up with constant interruptions
put up with being ignored
have to put up with it
won't put up with it any longer
ja: put up with the noise — 騒音を我慢する
put up with rude behavior — 失礼な振る舞いを我慢する
put up with constant interruptions — 何度も話を遮られるのを我慢する
put up with being ignored — 無視されるのを我慢する
have to put up with it — それを我慢しなければならない
won't put up with it any longer — これ以上は黙って受け入れない

en: I can put up with the noise during the day, but not when I’m trying to sleep.
Why should we have to put up with being interrupted every time we speak?
She made it clear that she wouldn’t put up with rude comments from clients.
Thanks for putting up with me while I was so stressed out.
ja: I can put up with the noise during the day, but not when I’m trying to sleep. — 昼間なら騒音を我慢できるけど、寝ようとしているときは無理だ。
Why should we have to put up with being interrupted every time we speak? — 発言するたびに話を遮られるのを、どうして我慢しなきゃいけないんだろう？
She made it clear that she wouldn’t put up with rude comments from clients. — 彼女は、取引先の失礼な発言を黙って受け入れるつもりはないと明言した。
Thanks for putting up with me while I was so stressed out. — 私がストレスでいっぱいいっぱいだったときに、付き合ってくれてありがとう。

usage.tone: Calling someone lazy can sound judgmental. I'm feeling lazy today usually refers to a temporary mood. A lazy afternoon can be enjoyable.

en: unwilling to work or make an effort
done with too little thought or effort
relaxed and unhurried, with little activity or effort
moving slowly or gently
ja: 働いたり努力したりするのを嫌がる、怠けた、面倒くさがりの
考えや手間をかけていない、手抜きの
のんびりした、ゆったり過ごす
ゆっくりと穏やかに動く

nuance.en: Lazy can criticize a person or their work, as in a lazy argument. With a day or activity, it often has a pleasant sense of doing very little. In programming, lazy evaluation means an expression is evaluated only when its result is needed.
nuance.ja: 人については「怠けている」、仕事や説明については「必要な手間や検討を省いている」という批判になりやすい。a lazy Sunday のように時間の過ごし方を表すときは、何もせずゆったり過ごす心地よさを表せる。プログラミングの lazy evaluation は、結果が必要になるまで式の評価を遅らせる「遅延評価」。

en: idle: Inactive or currently unused. An idle machine is simply sitting unused, while a lazy person is seen as unwilling to make an effort.
sluggish: Slow to move or respond, sometimes because of tiredness. Lazy usually suggests reluctance when applied to a person's effort.
laid-back: Relaxed and easygoing, especially as a personality trait. A laid-back coworker can still work very hard.
ja: idle：活動していない、使われていない状態。an idle machine は稼働していない機械。人を lazy と言うと、努力したがらないと評価する響きがある。
sluggish：動きや反応が鈍い。疲労などでも起こる。人の努力について lazy と言うと、やる気がないという含みが出やすい。
laid-back：気楽でおおらかな性格。a laid-back coworker は、穏やかな性格で仕事熱心な同僚にも使える。

note.en: More formal and usually critical when describing someone reluctant to work.
note.ja: 努力を嫌がる人を指す、より改まった批判的な語。

note.en: Close when describing an unhurried activity or pace.
note.ja: 急がずゆったりとした活動やペースを表すときに近い。

etymology.en: The related forms are lazily (adverb) and laziness (noun).
etymology.ja: 関連語は lazily（副詞）と laziness（名詞）。

en: feel lazy
be too lazy to cook
a lazy Sunday morning
a lazy breakfast
a lazy excuse
a lazy argument
a lazy river
lazy evaluation
lazy loading

be too lazy to cook — 料理するのが面倒だ
a lazy Sunday morning — のんびり過ごす日曜の朝
a lazy breakfast — ゆっくり楽しむ朝食
a lazy excuse — よく考えもせずにした言い訳
a lazy argument — 検討不足の主張
a lazy river — ゆったり流れる川
lazy evaluation — 遅延評価
lazy loading — 遅延読み込み

en: I was too lazy to cook, so I ordered dinner.
We spent a lazy Sunday morning drinking coffee and reading.
Blaming the users is a lazy excuse for a confusing design.
The page uses lazy loading to fetch images as they come into view.
ja: I was too lazy to cook, so I ordered dinner. — 料理するのが面倒で、夕食は出前を頼んだ。
We spent a lazy Sunday morning drinking coffee and reading. — 日曜の朝はコーヒーを飲んだり本を読んだりして、のんびり過ごした。
Blaming the users is a lazy excuse for a confusing design. — 分かりにくい設計を利用者のせいにするのは、ろくに考えていない言い訳だ。

grammar.countability: usually uncountable

usage.countability: Laziness normally has no plural. To describe one occasion, say a moment of laziness.

en: unwillingness to work or make an effort, either as a habit or on a particular occasion
a lack of care or thought in work that calls for more effort
ja: 働いたり努力したりするのを嫌がること、怠け癖、ものぐさ。一時的に面倒がることにも使う
必要な手間や思考を省くこと、手抜き、怠慢

nuance.en: Laziness typically implies that someone could make the effort but is unwilling to. Calling another person's behavior laziness can sound judgmental. Out of sheer laziness is often self-deprecating when someone admits taking a shortcut. Lazy can sound pleasant in a lazy Sunday, where a noun such as relaxation better captures that sense.
nuance.ja: やろうと思えばできることを面倒がってやらない、という評価が含まれやすい。人の行動を laziness と呼ぶと批判的に響く一方、自分のことを out of sheer laziness と言えば「まったくの面倒くさがりで」と自嘲気味に言える。a lazy Sunday のような心地よい「のんびり」を名詞で表すなら、relaxation などが自然。

en: idleness: A state of doing nothing or being inactive. Laziness usually attributes inactivity to unwillingness to make an effort.
procrastination: Putting a task off until later. It names the delay, which can stem from anxiety or perfectionism as well as laziness.
inertia: Continuing in the same state because starting or changing course is difficult. Laziness more directly suggests unwillingness to make an effort.
ja: idleness：何もしていないこと、活動していない状態。laziness は通常、努力したがらないことに焦点がある。
procrastination：やるべきことの先延ばし。先延ばしには面倒くささのほか、不安や完璧主義なども関わりうる。
inertia：始めたり方針を変えたりするのが難しく、そのままの状態が続くこと。laziness は労力をかけたがらないことをより直接的に表す。

note.en: A formal or literary term that can carry a strong moral judgment.
note.ja: 改まった、あるいは文学的な語で、道徳的な非難が強く出ることがある。

note.en: Close when judging how much work someone put into a particular task.
note.ja: 特定の作業にどれほど手をかけたかを評価する場合に近い。

etymology.en: Formed from lazy and the noun suffix -ness, with final y changing to i.
etymology.ja: lazy に名詞を作る接尾辞 -ness が付いた形。語末の y は i に変わる。

en: out of laziness
out of sheer laziness
a moment of laziness
accuse someone of laziness
put something down to laziness
intellectual laziness
ja: out of laziness — 面倒くささから
out of sheer laziness — 単に面倒くさくて
a moment of laziness — つい面倒になった一瞬
accuse someone of laziness — 人を怠けていると非難する
put something down to laziness — 何かの原因は怠けにあると考える
intellectual laziness — 自分で考えることを怠ること、知的怠慢

en: I ordered takeout out of sheer laziness, even though there was plenty of food in the fridge.
She put his missed deadlines down to laziness, but he was juggling three projects at once.
Repeating the claim without checking the evidence is a form of intellectual laziness.
ja: I ordered takeout out of sheer laziness, even though there was plenty of food in the fridge. — 冷蔵庫には食材がたっぷりあったのに、単に料理が面倒で出前を取った。
She put his missed deadlines down to laziness, but he was juggling three projects at once. — 彼女は彼が締切を何度も守れなかったのは怠けていたからだと思ったが、彼は三つの案件を同時に抱えていた。
Repeating the claim without checking the evidence is a form of intellectual laziness. — 証拠を確かめずにその主張を繰り返すのは、知的怠慢の一種だ。

usage.agreement: The verb normally agrees with the noun after of: There is plenty of food. There are plenty of seats.
usage.standalone: Use plenty on its own when the thing being counted or measured is clear: Do we need more rice? No, we have plenty.
usage.adverb: Plenty big enough means easily big enough. This use is informal, especially in American English.

en: a large amount or number of something, often as much as needed or more
(informal, especially US) quite, very, or easily, used to emphasize a description
(noun) a state of abundance
ja: たくさん、十分すぎるほどの量や数
（特に米の口語）かなり、とても、十分に。形容詞や副詞を強調する
（名詞）豊かさ、物資などが豊富な状態

nuance.en: Plenty of often reassures the listener that there is no shortage: We have plenty of time means there is no need to hurry. It can also simply emphasize a large number, even with something undesirable, as in plenty of problems.
nuance.ja: plenty of は「必要な分は十分にある」という余裕を伝えることが多い。We have plenty of time. なら「時間はたっぷりあるから、急がなくていい」という響き。plenty of problems のように、好ましくないことが数多くある場合にも使える。

en: enough: Reaches the amount needed. Plenty often suggests there is some to spare.
a lot of: Emphasizes a large quantity. Plenty of often measures that quantity against what is needed.
ample: Similar to plenty of when there is enough to spare, but more formal and used directly before a noun, as in ample time.
ja: enough：必要量に達している。plenty は余裕がある感じを出しやすい。
a lot of：量や数の多さに重点がある。plenty of は、必要な量を考えても十分にあるという含みを持ちやすい。
ample：余裕があることを表す改まった形容詞。ample time のように名詞の前に直接置く。

note.en: Close when plenty implies an amount beyond what is needed.
note.ja: 必要量を上回っているという含みがある場合に近い。

note.en: Close in casual speech when the emphasis is simply on a large quantity.
note.ja: 単に量や数が多いことを伝えるくだけた場面で近い。

etymology.en: Related to plentiful, meaning available in large quantities.
etymology.ja: 関連語の plentiful は「豊富な、たくさんある」という形容詞。

en: plenty of time
plenty of food
plenty of room
plenty of options
plenty of people
have plenty left
plenty big enough
a time of plenty
ja: plenty of time — たっぷりの時間
plenty of food — たっぷりの食べ物
plenty of room — 十分なスペース
plenty of options — たくさんの選択肢
plenty of people — 大勢の人
have plenty left — まだたっぷり残っている
plenty big enough — 余裕で十分な大きさだ
a time of plenty — 物資が豊かな時代

en: There was plenty of food in the fridge.
Take your time. We have plenty of time before the train leaves.
There are plenty of seats near the back.
Do we need more rice? No, we still have plenty.
This bag is plenty big enough for both laptops.
ja: There was plenty of food in the fridge. — 冷蔵庫には食材がたっぷりあった。
Take your time. We have plenty of time before the train leaves. — ゆっくりでいいよ。電車が出るまで時間はたっぷりある。
There are plenty of seats near the back. — 後ろの方には席がたくさん空いている。
Do we need more rice? No, we still have plenty. — お米を買い足す必要ある？ ううん、まだたっぷりあるよ。
This bag is plenty big enough for both laptops. — このバッグならノートパソコンが２台とも余裕で入る。

usage.tone: Purely speculative stresses the lack of confirmation. Highly speculative may refer to weak evidence or to substantial financial risk, depending on the noun.

en: based mainly on conjecture or possibilities, with limited confirming evidence
involving substantial financial risk in the hope of making a profit
ja: 推測に基づく、裏づけが乏しい、憶測の域を出ない
利益を期待して大きなリスクを取る、投機的な

nuance.en: A speculative explanation can be plausible, but the evidence is too limited to treat it as established. In speculative fiction, the word can instead describe the imaginative exploration of what might be. A speculative investment seeks profit under considerable uncertainty.
nuance.ja: speculative explanation はもっともらしい説明にも使えるが、確かな説明と見なすには裏づけが足りないという含みがある。speculative fiction では「もしも」を想像して描く作品を指す。speculative investment は大きな不確実性を引き受け、利益を狙う投資。

en: tentative: Provisional and open to revision. A tentative conclusion may already have some evidence behind it. Speculative emphasizes the role of conjecture.
hypothetical: Supposed for the sake of discussion. A hypothetical scenario may be deliberately imagined, regardless of how much evidence exists.
unsubstantiated: Lacking adequate supporting evidence. It is often a more direct criticism of a specific claim.
ja: tentative：暫定的で、あとから修正する余地がある。tentative conclusion は一定の証拠に基づくこともある。speculative は推測に頼る度合いに焦点がある。
hypothetical：議論のために仮定した。hypothetical scenario は、検討のために意図的に設定した仮の状況にも使う。
unsubstantiated：十分な裏づけがない。特定の主張を批判するときに、証拠不足をより直接的に指摘する。

note.en: A formal equivalent in the evidence-related sense.
note.ja: 推測に基づくという意味で近い、改まった語。

note.en: Close in finance, where speculative also suggests taking the risk in pursuit of profit.
note.ja: 金融の文脈で近い。speculative は利益を狙ってリスクを取る含みもある。

etymology.en: Related to speculate (verb) and speculation (noun), which also have both conjecture and finance senses.
etymology.ja: speculate（動詞）、speculation（名詞）と同じ語族。いずれも推測と投機の両方の用法がある。

en: a speculative claim
a speculative explanation
remain highly speculative
purely speculative
speculative fiction
a speculative investment
speculative trading
a speculative bubble
ja: a speculative claim — 推測に基づく主張
a speculative explanation — 推測に基づく説明
remain highly speculative — 依然として推測の域を出ない
purely speculative — まったくの推測にすぎない
speculative fiction — もしもの世界を描くフィクション
a speculative investment — 投機的な投資
speculative trading — 投機的な取引
a speculative bubble — 投機バブル

en: Without independent test results, any explanation for the failure remains speculative.
The link between the two events is plausible, but at this stage it’s still speculative.
The fund avoids highly speculative investments in companies with no revenue.
ja: Without independent test results, any explanation for the failure remains speculative. — 独立した試験結果がなければ、その不具合の原因についての説明はどれも推測の域を出ない。
The link between the two events is plausible, but at this stage it’s still speculative. — 二つの出来事に関連があるという見方はもっともらしいが、現段階ではまだ推測にすぎない。
The fund avoids highly speculative investments in companies with no revenue. — そのファンドは、売上のない企業への投機性の高い投資を避けている。

patterns: speculate on + a rise / fall in prices

usage.prepositions: Speculate about the cause introduces a topic for conjecture. Speculate in currencies refers to trading them for profit. Speculate on can occur in either sense, depending on what follows.

en: to suggest or consider possible explanations or outcomes without firm evidence
to take financial risks in pursuit of profit from expected changes in prices
ja: 確かな裏づけがない段階で、ありうる説明や結果を推測する、憶測する
価格の変動で利益を得ようとリスクを取る、投機する

nuance.en: Speculate often involves exploring possible explanations, sometimes in public. I don't want to speculate signals that the speaker is holding back because the facts are incomplete. In finance, speculating highlights the risks taken in anticipation of a price move.
nuance.ja: 考えられる説明を検討したり、公に推測を述べたりするのに使う。I don’t want to speculate. は、事実がまだ分からないので推測で発言するのは控えたい、という言い方。金融では、価格が動くと見込んでリスクを取ることに重点がある。

en: guess: An everyday word for giving an answer or estimate when you are unsure. Speculate often suggests considering possible explanations or outcomes.
infer: To reach a conclusion from clues or evidence. Speculate emphasizes the uncertainty or gaps in the evidence.
invest: A broad term for committing money in expectation of a return. Speculate highlights financial risk and expected price movements.
ja: guess：確信がないまま答えや見積もりを出すときの日常語。speculate は、ありうる説明や結果を考えるという響きが出やすい。
infer：手がかりや証拠から結論を導く。speculate は、不確実さや証拠の不足に重点がある。
invest：収益を期待して資金を投じる広い語。speculate は、価格変動を見込んでリスクを取ることを強調する。

note.en: A more formal equivalent for advancing an explanation without firm evidence.
note.ja: 裏づけの乏しい説明を示すという意味で近い、より改まった語。

etymology.en: Ultimately from Latin speculārī ‘to watch, observe’, related to specere ‘to look at’. The noun speculation is recorded in English in the late 14th century. The verb speculate is recorded from the 1590s and is often explained as a back-formation from that noun. Early English uses referred to contemplation. The sense of reasoning by conjecture came later, and the financial sense is recorded from the late 18th century.
etymology.ja: 語源をたどると、ラテン語 speculārī（見張る、観察する）に行き着く。これは specere（見る）と同系。英語では名詞 speculation が14世紀末に先に現れ、動詞 speculate は1590年代に記録されている。動詞は、既存の名詞から作られた形（逆成）とされる。初期の英語では「じっくり考える、思索する」の意味で使われ、後に「推測する」の意味が現れた。「投機する」の用法は18世紀後半に記録されている。

en: speculate about the cause
speculate about what happened
speculate that prices will fall
decline to speculate
speculate in currencies
speculate on a rise in oil prices
ja: speculate about the cause — 原因を推測する
speculate about what happened — 何が起きたかを推測する
speculate that prices will fall — 価格が下がると推測する
decline to speculate — 推測での発言を控える
speculate in currencies — 通貨に投機する
speculate on a rise in oil prices — 原油価格の上昇を見込んで投機する

en: Reporters speculated that the two companies were in merger talks.
I don’t want to speculate about the cause until we’ve seen the test results.
Some traders were speculating on a rise in oil prices.
ja: Reporters speculated that the two companies were in merger talks. — 記者たちは、両社が合併交渉をしているのではないかと推測した。
I don’t want to speculate about the cause until we’ve seen the test results. — 試験結果を見るまでは、原因について推測で話すのは控えたい。
Some traders were speculating on a rise in oil prices. — 原油価格の上昇を見込んで投機していたトレーダーもいた。

grammar.countability: usually uncountable (activity or talk) / countable for individual conjectures

usage.countability: News reports usually use the uncountable form: There has been widespread speculation. The plural speculations can refer to several individual conjectures.

en: the activity of forming or discussing ideas about what may be true or may happen without firm evidence, or an individual idea of this kind
financial activity involving risk in the hope of profiting from changes in prices
ja: 確かな裏づけがない段階で、何が事実か、今後何が起こるかを考えたり論じたりすること、推測、憶測。個々の推測を指すこともある
価格変動から利益を得ようとリスクを取る金融取引、投機

nuance.en: Fuel speculation is common in news writing when an event prompts more public conjecture. Mere speculation dismisses an idea as insufficiently supported. Market speculation refers to trading activity; speculation about a merger refers to conjecture even in a business article.
nuance.ja: 報道の fuel speculation は、ある出来事が憶測をさらに広げるときによく使う。mere speculation は、裏づけが足りず「単なる憶測にすぎない」という評価を示す。market speculation は市場での投機を、speculation about a merger は経済記事でも合併をめぐる憶測を指す。

en: rumor: An unconfirmed story or claim circulating among people. Speculation can be broader discussion about several possibilities.
hypothesis: A proposed explanation, often intended to be tested. Speculation highlights how uncertain or unconfirmed the idea is.
prediction: A statement about what will happen. Speculation can also concern events in the past and emphasizes uncertainty.
ja: rumor：人々の間で広まる、未確認の話や主張。speculation は、複数の可能性をめぐる議論にも使える。
hypothesis：提示された説明の仮説で、検証を前提とすることが多い。speculation は、その考えが未確認であることに焦点がある。
prediction：今後何が起きるかの予測。speculation は過去の出来事にも使え、不確かさが前面に出る。

note.en: Close when discussing an explanation without firm supporting evidence.
note.ja: 十分な裏づけのない推測という意味で近い。

etymology.en: The noun in the same word family as speculate and speculative.
etymology.ja: speculate（動詞）、speculative（形容詞）と同じ語族の名詞。

en: fuel speculation
spark speculation
widespread speculation
mere speculation
speculation about the merger
speculation that the CEO will resign
currency speculation
speculation in the housing market
ja: fuel speculation — 憶測をかき立てる
spark speculation — 憶測を呼ぶ
widespread speculation — 広く飛び交う憶測
mere speculation — 単なる憶測
speculation about the merger — 合併をめぐる憶測
speculation that the CEO will resign — CEOが辞任するのではないかとの憶測
currency speculation — 通貨投機
speculation in the housing market — 住宅市場での投機

en: The sudden resignation fueled speculation that the board was divided.
Without more data, that explanation is still mere speculation.
The report linked the sharp rise in house prices to speculation in the housing market.
ja: The sudden resignation fueled speculation that the board was divided. — 突然の辞任を受け、取締役会が内部分裂していたのではないかとの憶測が広がった。
Without more data, that explanation is still mere speculation. — さらにデータが得られないかぎり、その説明はまだ単なる憶測にすぎない。
The report linked the sharp rise in house prices to speculation in the housing market. — その報告書は、住宅価格の急騰を住宅市場での投機と結びつけた。

grammar.countability: usually uncountable (positioning or agreement); countable for a particular arrangement or grouping
patterns: the alignment of A with B

usage.prepositions: With identifies a reference point or goal. Between identifies the parties or things whose fit is being considered. On introduces the topic people agree on.

en: the arrangement or adjustment of things into the correct position or direction relative to one another
agreement or consistency between goals, policies, priorities, or actions
a grouping or relationship formed when people or groups take compatible positions
ja: 物の位置や向きを互いに合うように揃えること、位置合わせ、整列、調整
目標・方針・優先事項・行動などの一致、整合
人や集団が同じ方向を向くことによって生じる関係や勢力の配置

nuance.en: In physical contexts, alignment concerns position, angle, or orientation, as in wheel alignment and text alignment. At work, alignment can mean shared priorities among people or a fit between a plan and a goal. In AI, alignment concerns making system behavior accord with intended goals or values.
nuance.ja: 物理的な文脈では位置・角度・向きが揃っていること。wheel alignment は車輪の角度調整、text alignment は文字揃えを指す。仕事では、関係者の優先事項が揃うことや、計画と目標の整合を表す。AI alignment は、AIの振る舞いを意図された目標や価値観に沿わせることを指す。

en: agreement: Often focuses on a point people have agreed to. Alignment can describe a fit between things such as a budget and a strategy.
coordination: Organizing the timing or execution of activities. Alignment concerns whether they serve compatible goals.
consensus: Broad agreement within a group. Alignment can describe shared direction even when participants differ on details.
ja: agreement：人が何かに合意したことを指す場合が多い。alignment は予算と戦略のような物事同士の整合にも使える。
coordination：作業の時期や進め方を調整すること。alignment は、それぞれの作業が同じ方向の目標に沿っているかに焦点がある。
consensus：集団内で広く意見が一致していること。alignment は細部に意見の違いがあっても、方向性を共有している場合に使える。

note.en: Close when a policy or action fits a stated goal.
note.ja: 方針や行動が掲げた目標と整合する場合に近い。

note.en: Close in physical contexts, where alignment specifies the arrangement relative to a reference or another object.
note.ja: 物理的な文脈で近い。alignment は基準や他の物との位置関係に焦点がある。

etymology.en: Formed from align and the noun suffix -ment.
etymology.ja: align（揃える、方向を合わせる）に名詞を作る接尾辞 -ment が付いた形。

en: wheel alignment
text alignment
check the alignment
be out of alignment

alignment between teams
achieve alignment on priorities
political alignment
AI alignment

ja: Before we finalize the budget, we need to check its alignment with our long-term goals. — 予算を確定する前に、長期目標に沿っているか確認する必要がある。
The two teams reached alignment on what to deliver first. — 両チームは、何を先に納品するかについて認識を揃えた。

grammar.countability: countable (an individual conjecture) / uncountable (conjecture in general)

usage.countability: A conjecture is one specific proposition or explanation. Mere conjecture treats the ideas under discussion as unsupported supposition in general.

en: (noun) an explanation or conclusion put forward without enough evidence to establish it, or the forming of such ideas
(noun, mathematics) a proposition believed to be true that has yet to be proved or disproved
(verb) to propose or infer something on the basis of incomplete evidence
ja: （名詞）十分な裏づけがない段階で示す推測・推論、または推測すること
（数学の名詞）真であると予想されているが、まだ証明も反証もされていない命題、予想
（動詞）不十分な証拠や手がかりから推測する、推測を述べる

nuance.en: Conjecture is more formal than guess and often presents a specific idea for consideration. In mathematics, a conjecture may be supported by extensive computations or partial results. Its status depends on whether it has been proved, regardless of how persuasive that evidence is.
nuance.ja: guess より改まった語で、検討すべき具体的な推測を示すときによく使う。数学では、大規模な計算や部分的な結果に裏づけられていても、証明が得られるまでは conjecture（予想）と呼ぶ。日常の mere conjecture には「単なる憶測」という批判的な響きがある。

en: speculate: Often describes exploring or discussing possibilities. Conjecture as a verb is more formal and often introduces a particular tentative conclusion.
speculation: Common in news for ongoing conjecture or public discussion. A conjecture often singles out one specific proposition.
hypothesis: Often implies a proposed explanation or assumption to be tested. In mathematics, a conjecture is a proposition to be proved or disproved.
ja: speculate：複数の可能性を考えたり論じたりするときにも使う。動詞 conjecture はより改まっており、具体的な推測を提示するときによく使う。
speculation：報道などで、ある話題について飛び交う憶測をまとめて指せる。a conjecture は一つの具体的な推測や命題を取り上げることが多い。
hypothesis：検証するために置く仮説や前提を指すことが多い。数学の conjecture は証明や反証の対象となる予想。

note.en: Close for a tentative conclusion drawn from limited clues.
note.ja: 限られた手がかりから導いた推測という意味で近い。

etymology.en: From Old French conjecture or directly from Latin coniectūra ‘inference, interpretation’, from conicere ‘to throw together’. The Latin verb combines con- ‘together’ with iacere ‘to throw’. The literal sense suggests drawing scattered clues together to form a conclusion.
etymology.ja: 古フランス語 conjecture を経て、または直接、ラテン語 coniectūra（推論、解釈）から入った。もとは conicere（投げ集める）で、con-（一緒に）と iacere（投げる）からなる。散らばった手がかりを寄せ集めて結論を導く、と考えると意味をつかみやすい。

en: mere conjecture
put forward a conjecture
conjecture that something happened
formulate a conjecture
prove a conjecture
disprove a conjecture
ja: mere conjecture — 単なる憶測
put forward a conjecture — 推測を提示する
conjecture that something happened — 何かが起きたと推測する
formulate a conjecture — 予想を定式化する
prove a conjecture — 予想を証明する
disprove a conjecture — 予想を反証する

en: Without the original records, any explanation for the discrepancy is mere conjecture.

ja: Without the original records, any explanation for the discrepancy is mere conjecture. — 原記録がなければ、その食い違いをどう説明しても単なる憶測にすぎない。
The researchers conjectured that the two fragments came from the same manuscript. — 研究者たちは、二つの断片が同じ写本に由来すると推測した。

patterns: what A lacks in X, A makes up for in Y

usage.wordOrder: The thing being compensated for comes after for: make up for it, make up for missing the meeting. To name the method, add by + -ing.

en: to offset a lack, loss, or disadvantage
to do something to compensate for a mistake, disappointment, or missed opportunity
ja: 不足・損失・不利な点を補う、埋め合わせる
失敗や相手をがっかりさせたこと、逃した機会などの埋め合わせをする

nuance.en: A person can make up for a mistake by doing something helpful. A positive feature can also make up for a drawback, as when a great location makes up for a small room. To specify the person receiving the gesture, use make it up to someone.
nuance.ja: 人が何かをして失敗の埋め合わせをする場合にも、長所が短所を補う場合にも使う。たとえば、立地のよさが部屋の狭さを補うと言える。誰に埋め合わせをするかを示すなら make it up to someone を使う。

en: make it up to someone: Names the person you want to make amends to. Make up for names the mistake or loss being compensated for.
make up: Has several separate meanings. Make up missed work can mean doing the work you missed. Make up for missing work can mean compensating for the fact that you missed it.
offset: A more formal alternative, especially for costs, losses, or disadvantages.
ja: make it up to someone：埋め合わせをする相手を示す。make up for の後ろには、失敗や損失など埋め合わせの対象が来る。
make up：別の意味をいくつも持つ。make up missed work は、できなかった仕事をあとでこなすこと。make up for missing work は、仕事を休んだことによる影響などの埋め合わせをすること。
offset：より改まった語で、費用・損失・不利な点を相殺する場合によく使う。

note.en: Close for making good a loss or balancing a disadvantage, with a more formal tone.
note.ja: 損失や不利な点を補う場合に近く、より改まった響き。

etymology.en: The phrase uses make up in the sense of making good a shortage or loss. For introduces what is being compensated for.
etymology.ja: make up の「不足や損失を補う」の意味から理解できる。for の後ろに、何を補うのかを示す。

en: make up for lost time
make up for a shortfall
make up for the delay
make up for a mistake
make up for missing the meeting
more than make up for a drawback
ja: make up for lost time — 失った時間を取り戻す
make up for a shortfall — 不足分を埋める
make up for the delay — 遅れを取り戻す、遅れの埋め合わせをする
make up for a mistake — 失敗の埋め合わせをする
make up for missing the meeting — 会議を欠席したことの埋め合わせをする
more than make up for a drawback — 欠点を補って余りある

en: The room is small, but the view more than makes up for it.
I tried to make up for missing her birthday by taking her out to dinner the following weekend.
We worked through lunch to make up for lost time.
What the app lacks in polish, it makes up for in speed.
ja: The room is small, but the view more than makes up for it. — 部屋は狭いけれど、眺めのよさがそれを補って余りある。
I tried to make up for missing her birthday by taking her out to dinner the following weekend. — 彼女の誕生日を祝えなかった埋め合わせに、翌週末に彼女を食事に誘った。
We worked through lunch to make up for lost time. — 遅れを取り戻すため、昼休みも作業を続けた。
What the app lacks in polish, it makes up for in speed. — そのアプリは仕上がりの粗さを動作の速さで補っている。

usage.wordOrder: This verb is separable. Both iron out the wrinkles and iron the wrinkles out are possible. With a pronoun, say iron them out.

en: to remove wrinkles or creases with an iron
to resolve problems or differences, or settle outstanding details
ja: アイロンでしわや折りじわを伸ばす
問題や意見の食い違いを解消する、未決の細部を詰める

nuance.en: Figurative iron out often suggests working through specific obstacles so that a plan, agreement, or product works smoothly. It can imply that the overall direction is already set, as in iron out the remaining details. With differences, it suggests working toward agreement.
nuance.ja: 比喩では、計画や合意、製品がうまく機能するよう、具体的な障害を一つずつ解消する感じがある。iron out the remaining details は、大筋が決まった状態で「残っている細部を詰める」。differences が目的語なら、話し合いなどで意見の食い違いを解消すること。

en: sort out: Broadly means to organize, clarify, or resolve something. Iron out often suggests smoothing specific difficulties or settling details.
work out: Can mean finding a solution or devising a plan. Work out a plan can mean creating it, while iron out the details of a plan suggests refining it.
resolve: A more formal general verb for settling an issue or dispute. Iron out suggests working through points of friction.
ja: sort out：整理する、はっきりさせる、解決するなど幅広い。iron out は具体的な難点を解消したり、細部を詰めたりするときによく使う。
work out：解決策を見つけたり、計画を立てたりする。work out a plan は計画を作ること、iron out the details of a plan はその細部を詰めることを表せる。
resolve：問題や紛争を解決する改まった一般語。iron out には引っかかっている点を調整する感じがある。

note.en: Close for removing wrinkles or easing problems and irregularities.
note.ja: しわを伸ばす場合にも、問題やばらつきをならす場合にも近い。

etymology.en: The figurative use comes from the image of pressing wrinkles out of fabric with an iron.
etymology.ja: アイロンで布のしわを伸ばす動作から、問題や食い違いを解消して物事を円滑にするという比喩に広がった。

en: iron out the wrinkles
iron out the creases
iron out the remaining details
iron out the differences
iron out a few kinks
iron out the issues before launch
ja: iron out the wrinkles — しわを伸ばす、細かな問題を解消する
iron out the creases — 折りじわを伸ばす
iron out the remaining details — 残っている細部を詰める
iron out the differences — 意見の食い違いを解消する
iron out a few kinks — いくつかの不具合や難点を解消する
iron out the issues before launch — 公開前に問題を解消する

en: We agree on the main terms, but we still need to iron out a few details before signing.
The two teams met to iron out their differences over the release schedule.

ja: We agree on the main terms, but we still need to iron out a few details before signing. — 主要な条件には合意しているが、署名する前にまだ細部をいくつか詰める必要がある。
The two teams met to iron out their differences over the release schedule. — 両チームは、リリース日程をめぐる意見の食い違いを解消するために会合を開いた。
We found a few problems in testing and will iron them out before launch. — テストで見つかったいくつかの問題は、公開前に解消する予定だ。
Can you iron out the creases in this shirt? — このシャツの折りじわをアイロンで伸ばしてくれる？

usage.wordOrder: This verb is separable: flesh out the idea or flesh the idea out. With a pronoun, use flesh it out.

en: to develop a plan, idea, account, or character by adding details or substance
ja: 計画・アイデア・説明・登場人物などに具体的な内容を加え、肉付けする

nuance.en: Flesh out suggests that a basic structure is already in place. The added material may be examples, practical details, or a character’s motives and backstory.
nuance.ja: すでに骨格があり、事例や実施方法、登場人物の動機や過去などを書き足して、具体性や厚みを持たせるときに使う。

en: iron out: Resolve outstanding problems or differences. Flesh out a plan by adding substance, then iron out any issues that remain.
elaborate on: Explain a point in greater detail. Flesh out often involves building up a draft or outline by adding new material.
flush out: Drive something out of hiding or bring a hidden problem to light. The vowel is /ʌ/, while flesh has /e/.
ja: iron out：残っている問題や食い違いを解消する。計画を flesh out して具体化し、そこで残った問題を iron out すると言える。
elaborate on：ある点について詳しく説明する。flesh out は、下書きや骨子に材料を足して内容を充実させるときによく使う。
flush out：隠れているものを追い出す、潜在的な問題をあぶり出す。母音は /ʌ/ で、flesh は /e/。

note.en: A broader verb. Flesh out specifically suggests adding substance to something already sketched.
note.ja: より広い語。flesh out は、すでにある骨子に内容を足すことを示す。

etymology.en: The metaphor is that of adding flesh to a skeleton. The skeleton represents the basic structure, and the flesh represents the details that fill it out.
etymology.ja: 骨格に肉を付けるという比喩。骨格が大枠、肉がそこに加える具体的な内容にあたる。

en: flesh out an idea
flesh out a proposal
flesh out an outline
flesh out a character
flesh out the draft with examples
a fully fleshed-out plan
ja: flesh out an idea — アイデアを具体化する
flesh out a proposal — 提案に内容を肉付けする
flesh out an outline — 骨子に具体的な内容を加える
flesh out a character — 登場人物の描写に厚みを持たせる
flesh out the draft with examples — 事例を加えて草稿を充実させる
a fully fleshed-out plan — 細部まで具体化された計画

en: We have a rough outline for the proposal. Let’s flesh it out with a timeline and cost estimates.
The second draft fleshes out the main character by showing why she left home.
Once we’ve fleshed out the rollout plan, we can iron out any scheduling conflicts.
ja: We have a rough outline for the proposal. Let’s flesh it out with a timeline and cost estimates. — 提案の大枠はできている。日程案と費用の見積もりを加えて具体化しよう。
The second draft fleshes out the main character by showing why she left home. — 第2稿では、主人公が家を出た理由を描くことで、人物像に厚みを持たせている。
Once we’ve fleshed out the rollout plan, we can iron out any scheduling conflicts. — 導入計画を具体化したら、日程の重複や食い違いを調整できる。

usage.wordOrder: Both hash out the details and hash the details out work. With a pronoun, use hash them out.

en: to discuss something thoroughly, typically to settle an issue, reach an agreement, or decide the details
ja: 問題や条件についてじっくり話し合い、解決策・合意・具体的な内容を詰める

nuance.en: Hash out is informal and especially common in American English. It emphasizes the back-and-forth of working through different views or options. Let's hash it out invites a detailed discussion; we hashed out a deal describes the result of that discussion.
nuance.ja: 特に米語でよく使うくだけた表現。違う意見や選択肢を出し合い、話し合いながら結論を詰める過程に重点がある。Let’s hash it out. は「とことん話し合おう」、we hashed out a deal は「話し合いで合意をまとめた」。

en: iron out: Focuses on clearing up remaining problems or differences. Hash out emphasizes the discussion and can also describe negotiating the main terms.
flesh out: Adds substance or detail to an existing outline. Hash out suggests discussing what those details should be.
thrash out: A close equivalent, especially in British English, which can suggest vigorous debate.
ja: iron out：残っている問題や食い違いの解消に焦点がある。hash out はやり取りに重点があり、主要な条件を交渉して決める場合にも使える。
flesh out：すでにある骨子に内容を足して肉付けする。hash out は、その内容をどうするか話し合って決めることを示す。
thrash out：特にイギリス英語で近い表現。活発な議論を重ねる響きが出ることがある。

note.en: Close when working through an issue in conversation. Hash out often suggests aiming for a decision.
note.ja: 話し合いながら問題を検討する場合に近い。hash out は結論を出そうとする含みが出やすい。

etymology.en: The verb hash also means to chop into small pieces, as with food. In hash out, you can picture taking an issue apart and discussing it piece by piece.
etymology.ja: 動詞 hash には、食材などを細かく刻むという意味もある。問題を細かい論点に分けて、一つずつ話し合うとイメージすると覚えやすい。

equivalents.es: debatir a fondo / acordar los detalles

hash out the terms
hash out a deal
hash out a compromise
sit down and hash it out
ja: hash out the details — 細部を話し合って詰める
hash out the terms — 条件を交渉して決める
hash out a deal — 話し合って合意をまとめる

usage.object: Amplify is usually transitive. With voices, the object can refer to literal sound or, figuratively, to people’s views and experiences.

en: to make a sound louder or a signal stronger
to make an effect, feeling, or problem stronger, or make a message or viewpoint reach more people
to develop a statement or explanation by adding details, especially in formal use
ja: 音を大きくする、信号を増幅する
影響・感情・問題などを強める、メッセージや意見をより多くの人に届ける
（改まった用法）説明や発言に詳しい情報を加えて敷衍する

nuance.en: The object determines what grows. Amplify an effect means making its impact stronger. Amplify someone’s voice often means giving their views more visibility or reach, for example by sharing their message with a wider audience. Amplifying a message can spread it without changing its content.
nuance.ja: 何が大きくなるかは目的語で変わる。amplify an effect は「影響を強める」。amplify someone’s voice は、意見や経験がより多くの人に届くようにすること。amplify a message は、メッセージの内容自体を変えずに、拡散して届く範囲を広げる場合にも使う。

en: increase: Broadly means to make something greater in size or amount. Amplify often emphasizes greater strength, impact, or reach.
magnify: Can make something look larger, or make a problem or effect seem or become larger. Amplify is especially natural for sound, signals, and voices.
flesh out: Adds substance to an outline or draft. In its formal sense of elaborating, amplify can mean expanding a point already made.
ja: increase：大きさや数量を増やす広い語。amplify は強さ、影響、届く範囲が増すことを表しやすい。
magnify：物を拡大して見せたり、問題や影響を実際に、あるいは見かけ上大きくしたりする。amplify は音・信号・声と特に相性がよい。
flesh out：骨子や草稿に具体的な内容を肉付けする。改まった用法の amplify は、すでに述べた論点について説明を広げる場合にも使う。

note.en: Close when making a signal stronger or increasing a message’s reach.
note.ja: 信号を強くする場合や、メッセージの届く範囲を広げる場合に近い。

note.en: Close when making a feeling or effect stronger.
note.ja: 感情や影響を強めるときに近い。

etymology.en: Via Old French amplifier, from Latin amplificare ‘to enlarge’, built from amplus ‘large’ and a form of facere ‘to make’. Ample comes from the same Latin root amplus. The early English sense was to enlarge or expand.
etymology.ja: 古フランス語 amplifier を経て、ラテン語 amplificare（大きくする）から入った。amplus（大きな）と facere（作る、する）の結合形からなる。ample（十分な、広い）も同じ amplus に由来する。初期の英語では「大きくする、広げる」という意味だった。

usage.forms: Spoiled is standard in American English. British English uses both spoiled and spoilt.
usage.transitivity: Use spoil without an object when food goes bad, or with an object when something causes the damage: The milk spoiled. The heat spoiled the milk.

en: to damage something or make an experience less enjoyable, including by revealing part of a story too soon
to give someone too much of what they want, or to treat someone especially generously
to go bad and become unfit to eat or use, especially of food
(plural noun) goods taken from a defeated enemy, or rewards that come from a victory
ja: 何かを台無しにする、楽しみを損なう。物語の展開などを先に明かしてネタバレする場合にも使う
人の望みを聞きすぎて甘やかす。また、特別に手厚くもてなす
（特に食べ物が）傷む、腐る
（複数名詞 spoils）戦利品、勝利によって得られる利益や報酬

nuance.en: An unexpected interruption can spoil the mood without ruining the whole evening. Spoil a child often implies excessive indulgence. You’re spoiling me! can be a pleased reaction to generous treatment. Spoil the ending means revealing it and taking away the surprise. Spoilt for choice means having so many good options that choosing is difficult.
nuance.ja: spoil the mood は、その場の雰囲気を損なうこと。spoil a child は甘やかしすぎるという批判を含みやすいが、You’re spoiling me! は、手厚くもてなしてくれる相手に「こんなによくしてもらって」と喜びを込めて言える。spoil the ending は結末を先に明かして驚きを奪うこと。spoilt for choice は、よい選択肢が多すぎて迷うほど恵まれていること。

en: ruin: Typically stronger in everyday use and often suggests a more thorough loss. Spoil can mean making an experience less enjoyable.
go bad: An everyday equivalent when food spoils. Spoil also works transitively, as in Heat can spoil the milk.
indulge: To let someone have or do what they want, or to enjoy a treat oneself. Spoil a child more readily suggests a harmful effect from excessive indulgence.
ja: ruin：日常ではより強く響くことが多く、全体が台無しになる感じが出やすい。spoil は、楽しみがそがれる程度にも使える。
go bad：食べ物が傷むという日常表現。spoil は Heat can spoil the milk. のように、何かが食べ物を傷ませるという他動詞でも使える。
indulge：相手の好きにさせたり、自分で贅沢を楽しんだりする。spoil a child には甘やかしすぎの悪影響がにじみやすい。

note.en: Close when something makes an experience unpleasant or destroys its value.

note.en: Close when treating someone with extra care or luxury.
note.ja: 人を特別に手厚くもてなしたり、贅沢をさせたりする場合に近い。

etymology.en: From Anglo-French espoiller and ultimately Latin spoliare ‘to strip or plunder’, related to spolium ‘booty taken from an enemy’. Early English uses concerned stripping or plundering. The senses of ruining something and overindulging someone came later. The older sense is still visible in the spoils of war.
etymology.ja: アングロ・フランス語 espoiller を経て、ラテン語 spoliare（剥ぎ取る、略奪する）にさかのぼる。敵から奪った戦利品を表す spolium と同系。英語でも当初は剥ぎ取りや略奪を指し、のちに「台無しにする」「甘やかす」の意味が現れた。古い意味は the spoils of war（戦利品）に残っている。

usage.spelling: Demonetise is also used in British English.
usage.object: A platform can demonetize an individual video or a whole channel. With currency, the object is often a coin, banknote, or denomination.

en: to remove or disable the ability to earn money from content, a channel, or an account, especially on an online platform
to withdraw the status of a coin or banknote as legal tender
ja: 動画・チャンネル・アカウントなどの収益化を停止する、収益を得る資格を取り消す
硬貨や紙幣の法定通貨としての効力を失わせる

nuance.en: On a platform, demonetize often refers to removing eligibility for ad revenue or another platform payout. A demonetized video may still be available to watch. In the currency sense, old notes may still be exchangeable even after they cease to be legal tender, depending on the rules of the change.
nuance.ja: オンラインでは、広告収入など、プラットフォームを通じて収益を得る資格を取り消すことを指す場合が多い。収益化が停止された動画でも、引き続き視聴できる場合がある。通貨については、旧紙幣が法定通貨としての効力を失った後も、制度によっては新紙幣などに交換できる。

en: monetize: Enable or generate revenue from something. Demonetize reverses or removes that ability.
take down: Remove content from public access. Demonetize concerns the ability to earn revenue from it.
devalue: Reduce the value of a currency, especially against other currencies. Demonetize a banknote means to withdraw its legal-tender status.
ja: monetize：コンテンツなどから収益を得る、収益化する。demonetize はその収益化を取り消す。
take down：コンテンツを取り下げ、公開を止める。demonetize はコンテンツから収益を得られるかどうかに関わる。
devalue：特に他の通貨に対して通貨の価値を切り下げる。demonetize a banknote は、紙幣の法定通貨としての効力を失わせること。

note.en: A transparent alternative in the online-content sense.
note.ja: オンラインコンテンツの収益化を停止するという意味で言い換えられる。

note.en: An explicit paraphrase in the currency sense.
note.ja: 貨幣の法定通貨としての効力を失わせるという意味を明示した言い換え。

etymology.en: The word is recorded in English in the 19th century in the currency sense and comes from French. It is transparent as de- ‘remove or reverse’ plus monetize. The newer platform sense uses the modern meaning of monetize, ‘generate revenue from’.
etymology.ja: フランス語に由来し、英語では19世紀に通貨に関する用法が記録されている。「取り除く、元に戻す」を表す de- と monetize に分けて理解できる。オンラインでの用法は、monetize の現代的な意味「収益化する」を打ち消したもの。

usage.roles: The instructions confused me. I was confused about what to do. The instructions were confusing. Confused describes the person experiencing confusion, and confusing describes what causes it.
usage.direction: In I confused A with B, A is what I encountered and B is what I mistook it for. People often confuse A and B describes difficulty telling the two apart.

en: to make someone unsure about what something means or what to do
to wrongly identify one person or thing as another, or fail to distinguish between them
to make a situation or issue harder to understand by mixing things together or adding complication
ja: 人を混乱させる、意味や何をすべきか分からなくさせる
人や物を取り違える、区別すべきものを混同する
物事をごちゃ混ぜにしたり複雑にしたりして、状況や論点を分かりにくくする

nuance.en: Confuse someone often describes an ordinary moment of uncertainty, such as when instructions are unclear. Confuse A with B also applies to concepts: confusing correlation with causation means treating one as the other. Don't confuse A with B is often used to warn readers about that distinction.
nuance.ja: confuse someone は、説明が分かりにくくて戸惑うような日常的な場面でも使える。confuse A with B は人や名前だけでなく概念にも使い、confuse correlation with causation は「相関関係を因果関係と取り違える」。Don't confuse A with B. は、二つを区別するよう促す言い方。

en: mix up: A conversational alternative for muddling names, dates, or identities. I mixed up the dates means I got them wrong.
mistake A for B: Focuses on wrongly identifying A as B, often on a particular occasion.
puzzle: Makes someone wonder because something is difficult to explain. Confuse often suggests difficulty following information or deciding what to do.
ja: mix up：名前や日付などを取り違えるときの会話表現。I mixed up the dates. は「日付を取り違えた」。

puzzle：理由が分からず不思議に思わせる。confuse は情報についていけなかったり、どうすればよいか分からなかったりする場合にも使う。

note.en: Stronger when someone feels completely at a loss.
note.ja: 何が何だか分からず途方に暮れる場合の、より強い語。

note.en: More formal, especially when two distinct ideas are treated as one.
note.ja: 特に、別々の概念を一つのものとして扱ってしまうときの改まった語。

etymology.en: Ultimately from Latin confundere ‘to pour together, mix’, whose past participle was confusus. The English verb confuse arose later as a back-formation from confused. The Latin sense of mixing helps explain the modern idea of failing to keep things distinct.
etymology.ja: ラテン語 confundere（一緒に注ぐ、混ぜる）と、その過去分詞 confusus にさかのぼる。英語では confused から語尾を取り除く逆成によって、後から動詞 confuse が生まれた。「混ぜる」という語源は、別々の物事を取り違える意味につながる。

usage.context: A rigid frame can be a desirable design feature. A rigid policy often suggests that there is too little room for exceptions.

en: stiff and difficult to bend or deform
fixed and unwilling or difficult to change or adapt
stiff and motionless, especially because of fear or tension
ja: 硬くて曲がりにくい、変形しにくい
固定的な、柔軟性がない、融通が利かない
恐怖や緊張などで体がこわばった、身動きしない

nuance.en: Rigid emphasizes resistance to bending or change. A rigid frame holds its shape, which may be exactly what a design calls for. A rigid process can be predictable, but the word often suggests it handles unusual cases poorly. Someone who goes rigid with fear suddenly stiffens up.
nuance.ja: 曲げたり変えたりしにくいことに焦点がある。rigid frame は形が崩れにくい枠で、設計上の長所にもなる。rigid process は進め方が一定という面もあるが、例外に対応しにくいという批判を含みやすい。go rigid with fear は、恐怖で急に体がこわばること。

en: hard: Often describes a surface that resists indentation or scratching. Rigid describes resistance to bending or deformation.
stiff: Can describe something that bends only with effort, or muscles that are hard to move. Rigid generally suggests even less give.
strict: Describes firm enforcement of rules or high standards. Rigid emphasizes how difficult the rules or methods are to adapt.
ja: hard：押してもへこみにくい、表面に傷がつきにくいなどの硬さを表すことがある。rigid は曲がりにくさや変形しにくさに着目する。
stiff：力を入れないと曲がらない物や、動かしにくい筋肉にも使う。rigid はさらにしなりや動きが少ない感じを出しやすい。
strict：規則を厳しく守らせることや、基準が厳しいことに焦点がある。rigid は規則ややり方を状況に応じて変えにくいことを強調する。

note.en: Close for a rule, process, or attitude that leaves little room for adaptation.
note.ja: 調整の余地が少ない規則・手順・考え方を表す場合に近い。

note.en: Close for something that gives little under pressure, literally or figuratively.
note.ja: 物理的にも比喩的にも、力や圧力を受けてもほとんど譲らない場合に近い。

etymology.en: From Latin rigidus ‘stiff, hard, severe’, from rigēre ‘to be stiff’. The related English noun is rigidity, and the adverb is rigidly.
etymology.ja: ラテン語 rigidus（硬い、こわばった、厳しい）に由来し、そのもとは rigēre（こわばっている）。関連語は rigidity（名詞、剛性・硬直性）と rigidly（副詞）。

usage.prepositions: Strict with someone identifies the person expected to follow the rules. Strict about something identifies the rule or area where compliance matters.

en: requiring or enforcing close obedience to rules, standards, or limits
precise, exact, or narrowly defined
complete or absolute, especially when a condition is to be maintained
ja: 規則・基準・制限を厳しく守らせる、厳格な
